zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## 假日固定收益簡報

美國債市因獨立紀念日補假休市，日本最終春鬥結果卻強化了央行再升息的理由。連合旗下企業平均加薪5.01%，連續第三年超過5%；日本10年期殖利率升至2.81%，為1996年以來最高。油價回落已減輕美歐眼前升息壓力，日本仍有不同的國內條件。

假日期間的消息也讓市場關注，未來由誰承接政府債。法國預算協商困難，英國投資人偏好短債而非長債，澳洲AMP則降低退休組合的政府債配置。各自原因不同，但在央行與退休資金需求轉變時，都攸關主權發行人能否消化新供給。

信用融資仍有規劃中的收購債、境外借款，以及支持較小發行人的擔保。阿根廷把銀行附買回到期延至下一次總統大選之後，智利則提出可能改變大型本地買盤的退休金規則。美國重開市時，Fed升息急迫性較低，但最新非農之外，仍有不少融資與政策問題待觀察。

7月3日沒有美國固定收益交易時段或新的美債收盤。本篇涵蓋7月3日至7月6日亞洲早晨之間的資訊，海外交易與假日期貨提供的是開市背景，不是週五美債報酬。

## 全球利率、信用與主權債動態

### 日本薪資結果強化央行政策討論

連合旗下5,368家企業員工平均加薪5.01%，其中底薪增加3.5%。這是1989年至1991年以來，首次連續三年超過5%；連合代表約700萬名勞工。名目加薪不保證實質所得同幅提高，但支持薪資循環持續的看法，市場反映12月以前日本央行再升息機率約93%。

央行估計首季產出缺口0.53%，略低於0.57%，資本與勞動均有正貢獻。潛在成長估計由0.66%升至0.69%，但央行提醒兩者都受估計方法影響。財務大臣片山皋月重申，準備因應失序匯率變動，並把日債殖利率上升與美國政策訊號、偏弱就業及日本標售結果相連。10年期升至2.81%，顯示能源降價未消除通膨、財政及買盤疑慮。

### 歐洲通膨急迫性下降，預算工作卻更棘手

ECB委員Emmanuel Moulin表示，油價快速下跌改善了前景；6月一致通過升息25個基點至2.25%，當時並未把它定位為新一輪緊縮起點。Joachim Nagel仍要求警戒，Gabriel Makhlouf強調2%目標。先前歐元區通膨降至2.8%，減少立即再升息的必要，食品、服務與薪資的延後反應仍待確認。

Christine Lagarde依決策時資訊為6月升息辯護：外部衝擊已擴及能源以外，核心通膨由2.2%升至2.5%。第二輪效應雖未出現，仍須防範。其後停火與油價下跌改變展望，不必然代表當初決策錯誤；ECB仍預估2027年部分期間通膨高於目標。

法國5月製造業產出下降1.0%，前月修正為增加0.6%，主要弱項是運輸設備與電氣、電子及電腦產品。總工業產出僅降0.1%，礦業、能源與供水增加3.2%提供支撐。歐盟首季經常帳順差擴至€1,134億、占GDP 2.4%，服務及初次所得改善，抵銷商品順差減少。法國生產偏弱，並不等同歐洲外部融資全面承壓。

法國財政協商則是另一項風險。財長Roland Lescure希望赤字接近GDP的5%，只略低於2025年5.1%。總理Sebastien Lecornu警告，若沒有新財政法案而只延用既有立法，赤字可能達6.5%。2027年預算須通過分裂國會，4月又有總統大選。官員表示發債及標售仍順利，問題在於政治協議能否帶來可信的未來借款路徑。

英國最近完成交易時段的2年與10年期利差擴至66個基點，為3月中以來最陡收盤，也高於可比較美、德曲線。資產管理業者願意承接高殖利率短債，卻因退休金需求減少、未來預算細節未定而不願延長天期。曲線並非只反映眼前英國央行降息預期。

### 傳統買方重新考慮政府債配置

2月管理A$1,620億的AMP，在過去六至十二個月移除年輕成員退休組合的政府債，其他組合也減碼，轉向公司債、商品及農業。通膨與股債相關性提高，削弱了主權債的分散效果。這是一家機構的配置決策，不能推成所有澳洲投資人都退出政府債。

智利監理機關則為近$2,600億退休金資產提出生命週期規則，讓年長成員增加高品質本地政府與公司債，減少股票、高收益、新興市場債及另類資產。如果採用，即使主權供給不變，本地需求也可能重新分配。

丹麥呈現另一種制度影響。央行維持歐元聯繫匯率，透過龐大的擔保債市場影響家庭借款成本，其政策利率比ECB低40個基點。影響來自匯率制度與本地房貸融資，而非單一外匯變動的大小。

中國6月淨買政府債人民幣100億，低於5月500億，為九個月最低。新隔夜公開市場操作讓人民銀行更精準調度資金，不必同樣依賴較長天期政府債購買，即可供應短期現金。支持流動性與支持債券價格，因而可以分開處理。

### 收購債與擔保維持信用融資管道

CVC計畫夏季之後發行€12億高收益債，替換收購義大利食品原料商Irca的過橋融資，另搭配循環額度。在仍以再融資與重新定價為主的市場，這將增加槓桿收購供給。ICICI Bank則考慮未來幾週依全球中期票據計畫籌至少$5億，利用印度央行吸引境外資本的外匯交換優惠。兩筆計畫都尚未確定最終成交條件。

渣打為African Frontier Capital安排$5,000萬四年期綠色債，Green Guarantee Co.保證支持惠譽BBB評估。這種方式旨在使$5,000萬至$1億的交易，也能吸引已開發市場買方，讓未達指標規模的中型能源及農業企業取得債市資金。擔保容量與項目現金流仍是關鍵，並非證明借款人已能無擔保發債。

阿根廷把三筆國際銀行附買回合併為$60億額度，2028年9月到期，移至2027年總統大選之後；原本該選舉年有逾$200億到期。展延降低近期付款集中度，但7月仍有逾$40億支付，持續回到無擔保國際市場的能力也尚未證明。

土耳其6月CPI月增0.99%、年增32.11%，食品通膨35.45%，住宅及公用事業45.14%，顯示能源緩解後國內價格壓力仍大。利差交易投資人則因美國政策與美元不確定性，將資金來源分散到歐元、加幣及日圓。多幣別可減少依賴單一來源，無法隔絕全球利差變化。

### Fed治理與假日市場

最高法院阻止免除Lisa Cook職務後，川普盟友據報仍研究其他撤換Fed理事的方法，使獨立性問題重新受到注意。偏弱非農此前已降低即刻升息預期，新增治理消息關係的是未來決策如何形成，並與Warsh減少前瞻指引的偏好並行。美債休市期間，不能據此認定期限溢價已實際上升。

假日風險資產較強。Nasdaq 100期貨上漲1.2%，亞洲股市漲約2%，黃金漲1.2%至約$4,170。布蘭特低於$72，市場衡量荷莫茲持續通行與美伊談判。這些是海外及期貨觀察，市場首次完全反映的Fed升息25個基點，仍由10月移至12月，提供週一開盤背景，而非新的美國現貨收盤。

## 下個交易時段觀察

美國7月6日週一美東10:00恢復公布資料，包括ISM服務業及紐約Fed全球供應鏈壓力指數。週二有5月貿易及6月消費者預期，週三14:00公布6月16日至17日FOMC紀錄。服務業活動與價格將檢驗非農放緩是否擴及其他部門，家庭預期與會議紀錄則釐清升息理由還剩多少。

財政部週一標售$920億91天期、$790億182天期；週二有$900億42天期、$520億364天期及$580億3年期。週三增額$390億票息4.375%的10年期，週四增額$220億票息5.000%的30年期。投標參與、交易商留債及次級表現，將協助區分例行現金管理與長天期需求不足。

日本5月勞動初值7月7日公布，接續6月央行操作、政府交易及5月消費指數，區域經濟報告9日公布。現金薪資與實質薪資將顯示強勁協商結果如何進入家庭所得；消費與各地物價則有助判斷，低油價下政策正常化是否仍能推進。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Holiday Fixed-Income Brief

Japan's final spring wage settlement strengthened the case for further BOJ tightening while US bond markets were shut for the observed Independence Day holiday. Workers at Rengo-affiliated companies secured an average 5.01% increase, the third consecutive year above 5%. Japanese 10-year yields reached 2.81%, their highest since 1996, despite the retreat in oil that had eased immediate rate-hike expectations in the US and Europe.

The holiday news also drew attention to who would buy sovereign debt. France faced a difficult budget negotiation, UK investors preferred short gilts over longer maturities, and Australia's AMP had cut government-bond allocations in retirement portfolios. These were different developments, but all mattered to issuers relying on investors to absorb supply as traditional central-bank and pension demand changed.

Credit funding was still available through planned buyout bonds, offshore borrowing and guarantees for smaller borrowers. Argentina extended bank-repo maturities beyond its next presidential election, while Chile proposed pension rules that could redirect a large domestic buyer base. The next US session would reopen with less urgency around a Fed hike, but plenty of financing and policy questions beyond the latest payroll report.

There was no July 3 US fixed-income session or new Treasury close. This edition covers the period from Asia morning July 3 through Asia morning July 6; overseas trading and holiday futures provide reopening context, not a Friday US bond return.

## Global Rates, Credit, And Sovereign Developments

### Japan's Pay Settlement Reinforces the BOJ Debate

Workers at 5,368 Rengo-affiliated companies won a 5.01% average pay increase, including 3.5% in base pay. It was the first three-year run above 5% since 1989–1991. Rengo represents about 7 million workers. The result did not guarantee the same gain in real household income, but it strengthened evidence of a sustained wage cycle. Markets assigned about a 93% probability to another BOJ increase by December.

The BOJ estimated a first-quarter output gap of 0.53%, slightly below 0.57%, with positive contributions from capital and labor. Estimated potential growth rose to 0.69% from 0.66%; the bank cautioned that both measures depend on methodology. Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama reiterated readiness to respond to disorderly currency moves and linked higher JGB yields to US policy signals, weak US labor data and the soft domestic auction. The 10-year's rise to 2.81% showed that lower energy costs had not displaced concerns about inflation, fiscal plans and bond demand.

### Europe Has Less Inflation Urgency but More Budget Work

ECB member Emmanuel Moulin said falling oil had improved the outlook after June's unanimous quarter-point increase to 2.25%. The decision had not been presented as the start of a tightening cycle. Joachim Nagel still urged vigilance and Gabriel Makhlouf stressed the 2% target. The earlier euro-area inflation decline to 2.8% made an immediate follow-up less compelling, while leaving the delayed effect on food, services and wages unresolved.

Christine Lagarde defended the June decision on the evidence then available. The external shock had spread beyond energy and core inflation had risen from 2.2% to 2.5%. Second-round effects had not appeared, but were still a risk. The ceasefire and subsequent oil decline changed the outlook without necessarily invalidating the original decision; the ECB's projection still put inflation above target into 2027.

French manufacturing output fell 1.0% in May after a revised 0.6% gain, led by transport equipment and electrical, electronic and computer goods. Total industrial output slipped only 0.1%, cushioned by a 3.2% increase in mining, energy and water. The EU's first-quarter current-account surplus widened to €113.4 billion, or 2.4% of GDP, as services and primary income outweighed a smaller goods surplus. Weak French production did not amount to broad European external-funding stress.

France's fiscal negotiations posed a separate risk. Finance Minister Roland Lescure sought a deficit close to 5% of GDP, only slightly below 2025's 5.1%. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu warned that rolling over legislation without a new finance bill could lift it to 6.5%. The 2027 budget faced a fragmented parliament and an April presidential election. Officials said issuance and auctions were working well; the question was whether a political agreement could deliver a credible path for future borrowing.

In the latest completed UK session, the two-/10-year gilt slope widened to 66 basis points, its steepest close since mid-March and steeper than comparable US and German curves. Asset managers were willing to buy short maturities at elevated yields but reluctant to extend duration as pension demand weakened and future budget details remained unresolved. The slope reflected more than expectations of a near-term BOE cut.

### Traditional Buyers Reconsider Government Bonds

AMP, which managed A$162 billion in February, had removed government bonds from younger members' retirement portfolios and cut allocations elsewhere over six to 12 months. It favored corporate credit, commodities and agriculture as inflation and higher stock-bond correlation weakened the diversification case for sovereigns. That was a portfolio-allocation decision, not evidence that all Australian institutions were abandoning government debt.

Chile's regulator proposed life-cycle rules for nearly $260 billion of pension assets. Older members would move toward high-quality domestic government and corporate bonds and away from equities, high yield, EM debt and alternatives. If adopted, the proposal could reshape local demand even without a change in sovereign issuance.

Denmark highlighted a different institutional influence. Nationalbanken's defense of the euro peg passes through a large covered-bond market into household borrowing costs, with its policy rate 40 basis points below the ECB's. The currency regime and local mortgage financing determine that transmission, rather than the size of any isolated foreign-exchange move.

China reduced net government-bond purchases to 10 billion yuan in June from 50 billion in May, the smallest amount in nine months. A new overnight open-market operation gave the PBOC a more precise funding tool. It could supply short-term cash without relying as heavily on longer-duration sovereign purchases, separating support for liquidity from support for bond prices.

### Buyout Supply and Guarantees Keep Credit Routes Open

CVC planned €1.2 billion of high-yield bonds after the summer to replace bridge financing for its purchase of Italian ingredients producer Irca, alongside a revolving facility. The deal would add buyout supply to a market still dominated by refinancing and repricing. ICICI Bank was considering at least $500 million under its global medium-term-note program in coming weeks, using an RBI foreign-exchange swap concession to attract offshore capital. Neither prospective transaction had established final clearing terms.

Standard Chartered placed a $50 million four-year green bond for African Frontier Capital. A Green Guarantee Co. backstop supported Fitch's BBB assessment. The approach aimed to make $50 million–$100 million issues investable for developed-market buyers, potentially extending access to mid-sized energy and agricultural companies below benchmark scale. Guarantee capacity and project cash flow remained central; the deal did not establish unsecured market access for the underlying borrowers.

Argentina combined three international-bank repos into a $6 billion facility due September 2028, moving maturities beyond the 2027 presidential election. More than $20 billion had previously been due in that election year. The extension reduced a near-term concentration of payments, but over $4 billion still fell due in July and the country had yet to demonstrate durable access to unsecured international borrowing.

Turkey's June CPI rose 0.99% monthly and 32.11% annually. Food inflation was 35.45% and housing and utilities 45.14%, underscoring how much domestic inflation remained after energy relief. Carry investors were diversifying funding from dollars into euros, Canadian dollars and yen as uncertainty about US policy and the dollar increased. Multiple funding currencies reduced dependence on one source, without insulating borrowers from changes in global rate differentials.

### Fed Governance and Holiday Trading

Reports that Trump allies were exploring further ways to remove Fed governors after the Supreme Court blocked the effort against Lisa Cook reopened questions about independence. The earlier soft payroll report had already reduced immediate hike expectations. The new governance issue concerned how future decisions would be made, alongside Warsh's preference for less forward guidance; neither development established a realized increase in Treasury term premium during a closed market.

Holiday trading was firmer in risk assets. Nasdaq 100 futures rose 1.2%, Asian equities gained about 2% and gold advanced 1.2% to roughly $4,170. Brent held below $72 as investors weighed continued Hormuz flows and US-Iran talks. These were overseas and futures observations, with the first fully priced Fed quarter-point increase still shifted from October to December. They provided Monday's starting context rather than a new US cash close.

## Next Open-Session Watch

US releases resume Monday, July 6 at 10:00 ET with ISM services and the New York Fed Global Supply Chain Pressure Index. May trade and the June Survey of Consumer Expectations follow Tuesday; minutes of the June 16–17 FOMC meeting arrive Wednesday at 14:00. Services activity and prices will show whether the payroll slowdown extends beyond hiring, while household expectations and the minutes help assess the remaining case for a rate increase.

Treasury sells $92 billion of 91-day and $79 billion of 182-day bills Monday. Tuesday adds $90 billion of 42-day bills, $52 billion of 364-day bills and a $58 billion three-year note. Wednesday brings a $39 billion reopening of the 4.375% 10-year note; Thursday follows with $22 billion of the 5.000% 30-year bond. Bidder participation, dealer retention and secondary performance will distinguish routine cash management from weak demand for longer duration.

Japan's May provisional labor data arrive July 7, followed by June BOJ operations, government transactions and the May consumption index. The regional economic report is due July 9. Cash earnings and real wages will show how the strong negotiated pay settlement reaches households; consumption and regional price evidence will help determine whether normalization can proceed despite cheaper oil.

overall_summary.headline: Japan's pay gains and changing bond buyers set the reopening agenda
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Japan's final wage settlement delivered a third year of increases above 5%, supporting further BOJ tightening even as lower oil eased immediate US and European policy pressure. Ten-year JGB yields reached 2.81%. US fixed-income markets were closed July 3 for the observed Independence Day holiday.

France faced difficult budget negotiations, UK buyers preferred shorter gilts and AMP cut government bonds from some retirement portfolios. Chile's proposed pension rules pointed in the other direction for older savers, potentially increasing demand for high-quality domestic bonds.

CVC and ICICI prepared new financing, a guaranteed African green bond illustrated access below benchmark scale, and Argentina extended bank repos beyond its presidential election. Services data, Treasury auctions and Japanese income releases will shape the next open sessions.
overall_summary.summary: Rengo's final wage increase reached 5.01%, while fiscal negotiations and shifting institutional allocations kept sovereign demand in focus. There was no new US Treasury close.
